sentences.text:
This is the first application filed by the applicant under Section 439 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 for grant of regular bail relating to Crime No. 594/2023 registered at Police Station Raipuria, District Jhabua (M.P.) for the offence under Sections 376, 450, 506 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860.
2.

As per prosecution story, on 30.9.2023 prosecutrix lodged an FIR at police station Raipuria by stating that on 29.9.2023 at about 10 pm she was sleeping inside her house alongwith her minor children, at that time applicant entered into her house and committed rape upon her and threatened her that if she discloses the incident to anyone then he will kill her.
On the next day she narrated the incident to her father and thereafter lodged the FIR.
Accordingly, offence has been registered against the applicant.
3. Learned counsel for the applicant submits that the applicant is an innocent person and he has been falsely implicated in this offence.

The applicant is a married,

sentences.text: matured and major lady, MLC of prosecutrix is not supported the case of prosecution and FIR is belated, applicant is permanent resident of Jhabua district.
Final conclusion of the trial is likely to take sufficient long time.
Under the above circumstances, prayer for grant of bail may be considered on such terms and conditions, as this Court deems fit and proper.

4. Per contra, learned counsel for the respondent / State opposes the bail application and prays for its rejection by submitting that prosecutrix has supported the case of prosecution in her statement under section 164 Cr.P.C.
5. Perused the impugned order of the trial Court as well as the case diary.
6. After considering all the facts and circumstances of the case, nature and gravity of offence,
arguments advanced by the learned counsel for the applicant and also taking note of the fact that prosecutrix is a major and married lady, FIR is belated, MLC is not supported the case of prosecution, investigation is over and charge sheet has been field, therefore, no further custodial interrogation of applicant is required, and final conclusion of the trial will take sufficient long time, I deem it proper to release the applicant on bail.
Therefore, without commenting on the merits of the case, the application is allowed.

7. It is directed that applicant be released on bail on his furnishing personal bond in the sum of Rs.75,000/- (Rupees Seventy Five Thousand Only) with one solvent surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial Court for his appearance before the trial Court, as and when required.

He shall abide by all the conditions enumerated under Section 437(3) Cr.P.C.
Certified copy as per rules.

(ANIL VERMA) JUDGE BDJ Rakesh vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 18 December, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/168979367/
